classification.difficultyReason: Introduce an altitude and apply exact trigonometric ratios in two right-angled triangles.

content.prompt: Find the exact value of $x$ in each diagram. No calculators required.

spec.description: Unshaded triangle with horizontal base, upper vertex, left side 6, right side x, and base angles 60° and 45°.
spec.mathematics: The side 6 is opposite 45°; x is opposite 60°. Coordinates are derived from the stated base angles.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens; no altitude or answer.

answer.short: $x=3\sqrt6$. Draw an altitude and use the exact sine ratios.
answer.worked:
Draw the perpendicular height $h$ from the upper vertex to the base.
$$\begin{align*}\sin60^\circ&=\frac{h}{6}\\h&=6\times\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\h&=3\sqrt3\\\sin45^\circ&=\frac{3\sqrt3}{x}\\x&=\frac{3\sqrt3}{1/\sqrt2}\\x&=3\sqrt6\end{align*}$$

answer.short: $x=3\sqrt2$. Draw an altitude and use the exact sine ratios.

$$\begin{align*}\sin30^\circ&=\frac{h}{6}\\h&=6\times\frac12\\h&=3\\\sin45^\circ&=\frac{3}{x}\\x&=\frac{3}{1/\sqrt2}\\x&=3\sqrt2\end{align*}$$
